questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Explain the principle of indirect rule
questions.stem: A study group revision asks what indirect rule meant in Nigeria. Provide a model answer.

answer.exemplar: Indirect rule governed through existing local chiefs and institutions under British supervision, reducing administrative costs and leveraging traditional authority. British officials set policy while chiefs enforced it, blending colonial control with indigenous structures.

questions.explanation: Indirect rule used local chiefs as intermediaries under British oversight. It saved costs and harnessed traditional authority while maintaining colonial control.

questions.stem: A study group revision asks why a metropole might prefer a protectorate. Provide a model answer.

answer.exemplar: A protectorate cost less to administer because local rulers handled daily governance, while the metropole controlled foreign affairs and defense. It offered imperial influence without the expense of direct colonial bureaucracy.

questions.explanation: Protectorates cost less because local rulers governed daily while the metropole controlled foreign affairs and defense.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a source on company rule

stimulus.body: The company raised private capital, administered territory, and collected revenue under its charter. When profits fell, it cut spending on welfare and infrastructure, provoking unrest. The state eventually intervened, citing mismanagement and humanitarian concerns.

questions.stem: A study group revision reads this source. What does it best support?

options.text: The company invested heavily in welfare
Private rule prioritized profit and neglected welfare

questions.explanation: The source shows profit-driven cuts to welfare and state intervention after mismanagement. It supports private prioritization of profit, not welfare investment or non-intervention.
